project: BTRC P1 — Inject Roots and External Effects Once Through Canonical Wire
description: Implement packet P1 so root.BuildProcess and canonical pkg/wire select exact service roots and external-effect owner ports once, runtime operations carry values and opaque IDs only, dynamic logging and metrics destinations remain private owner scope state, repeated sessions reuse injected instances, and process construction stays inert.

context.customerAsk: Implement packet P1 of the build-time-runtime-composition plan: project edges.Edges into exact owner ports in canonical Wire, pass peer root interfaces directly to consumers, replace per-operation logger, metrics, runner, store, client, and observer parameters with build-time owner dependencies, and make dynamic log/metric file selection private scope state. Do not wait for P0; classify dependencies while migrating them and consult its matrix if published. Keep the critical-path lane in small, mergeable steps.
context.problem: Runtime opening still acts as a secondary composition path: operation-time inputs can carry behavioral collaborators, grouped dependencies, external-effect bags, and per-session logger or metrics factories. Sessions can therefore use newly selected or rebound instances instead of the process roots and edges supplied through BuildProcess, obscuring ownership, weakening functional overrides, coupling contracts to implementations, and risking construction-time side effects.
context.solution: Classify each migrated dependency as a build-time owner dependency, operation value, or private owner state; project edges.Edges once into exact owner ports; inject narrow peer roots directly; make operation contracts value-and-ID only; move dynamic observability destinations behind the injected logging and metrics owners; and prove instance reuse, session isolation, functional overrides, compatibility, and inert construction.

baselineFailures.evidence: The latest-head initial run and failed-job retry reproduce the unchanged assertion: current structured API-server diagnostics precede SERVER_BIND_FAILED, while the untouched test expects the legacy migration warning followed by one diagnostic line. The P1 diff is empty for this package, and the same mismatch reproduces locally on Windows.

acceptanceCriteria: root.BuildProcess and canonical Wire select each migrated service root and external-effect implementation once, inject exact owner ports, and provide the same instances to every consuming session path.

Two sequential or concurrent Factory Session starts use the same injected service-root and edge instances while retaining distinct session/runtime identities, logging/metrics scopes, results, and lifecycle state.

Start, invoke, activate, replay, direct-execution, and related operation contracts carry immutable values, configuration selections, and typed opaque IDs only; they do not carry services, factories, dependency/effect bags, loggers, metrics recorders, stores, clients, runners, observers, or dependency-injection callbacks.

Functional effect overrides are supplied only through root.BuildProcess and edges.Edges, reach the exact permanent owner, and are used unchanged by every relevant operation without runtime rebinding or fallback construction.

Dynamic log and metric file selection is owner-private scope state behind one injected logging/metrics implementation, with collision-free session destinations, explicit close behavior, and no session logger or recorder factory exposed to callers.
Building the process is inert and existing successful and failed customer flows retain equivalent terminal results and canonical event behavior after explicit activation.

Typecheck, focused package and root-process tests, make verify-fast, and required CI pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared/generated-file churn are resolved against current origin/main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Establish exact build-time owner contracts

acceptanceCriteria: Every dependency migrated in this packet is classified as a build-time owner dependency, an operation value, or private owner state, with one named owner and no ambiguous duplicate ownership.

If the P0 ownership matrix is published before this story merges, P1 classifications are reconciled with it; any necessary deviation is documented with its owner and behavior rationale without waiting for P0 to finish.

Each affected service accepts only the narrow peer-root interfaces and external-effect ports it actually consumes, and no new dependency bag, service locator, child injector, or callback-based construction contract is introduced.
A construction test supplies distinct fakes for owner ports and proves each service receives the intended instance without invoking it.

acceptanceCriteria: Canonical Wire projects each migrated edges.Edges field directly into the exact permanent owner port and resolves any default once during process construction.
A replacement supplied to root.BuildProcess is the instance observed by each relevant owner operation across two session starts; runtime input cannot replace, wrap, or reconstruct it.
Missing required effects fail process construction with an actionable owner-specific error before activation, while valid effects remain uncalled during construction.
Functional override evidence enters through root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute and observes calls on the injected edge without importing runtime-opening configuration or creating a second graph.
Focused edge-projection and root-process functional tests pass.

Runtime opening no longer accepts the aggregate external-effect bag; fixed ports win over operation observation fallbacks. Construction omission/identity tests, edge projection/default tests, root BuildProcess + Process.Execute provider override evidence, focused Factory Sessions/Wire/root tests, make test, make wire-smoke, make verify-fast, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, and git diff checks pass. userStories.title: Share peer service roots across session operations
userStories.description: As a customer starting multiple Factory Sessions, I want every session coordinator and runtime consumer to call the same injected peer roots so that starting a session does not create or discover another service graph.
acceptanceCriteria: Factory Sessions and other affected consumers receive their peer service-root interfaces directly from canonical Wire and retain those roots for all operations.
Two sequential and two concurrent session starts call the same injected root instances while receiving distinct session/runtime identities and isolated owner-private state.
Starting, invoking, replaying, or directly executing a session does not call a production service/infrastructure constructor, child injector, service locator, or stored service factory.
Failure in one session operation does not replace, mutate, or close the shared process-scoped roots used by another session.
Focused root-identity, concurrent-session, and failure-isolation tests pass, including race or repeat coverage for shared-root access.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented one process-scoped Factory Sessions root with the selected clock and its owner-private runtime assembly constructed during canonical Wire composition. Runtime opening retains the exact root and consumes the direct runtime capability; it no longer calls Service.ForRuntime or creates a child Factory Sessions assembly. Added construction identity coverage, direct-root identity coverage, concurrent two-operation failure isolation with race/repeat coverage, and private Models-scope close assertions. The compatibility ForRuntime method remains inert and returns the same root for callers not yet migrated; it is not used by runtime opening. pkg/services/factory_sessions/... tests, make test, make wire-smoke, make verify-fast, root/support tests, focused race coverage, and package structure/maintainability/file-count gates pass. make lint still stops at the unchanged pkg-boundary migration baseline documented in progress.txt. Stories 004-006 remain pending.

userStories.title: Make runtime operations value-and-ID only
userStories.description: As a service consumer, I want runtime operations to exchange values and opaque identities only so that calling an operation cannot finish dependency injection or expose implementation handles.
acceptanceCriteria: Affected Start, Invoke, Activate, replay, and direct-execution requests contain only immutable domain values, selections, and typed opaque IDs needed for the operation.

Affected operation requests and results no longer accept or return loggers, metrics recorders, runners, stores, clients, observers, services, factories, grouped dependencies/effects, or generic callbacks.

Existing valid requests retain their terminal results, response behavior, and canonical Factory Event order, and invalid requests retain actionable typed failure behavior without invoking an external effect.
CLI, HTTP, MCP, and internal callers that exercise a changed operation translate boundary data into the same value-only owner request rather than constructing a collaborator.
Focused operation-contract and compatibility tests pass; authored OpenAPI sources and generated clients are updated only if a customer-facing contract must change.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completed the value-and-ID operation cutover. Previous iterations detached InvocationTarget, invocation-only and execution-only runtime opening requests, and the application-opening resolver/CLI runner from per-call loggers and metrics recorders. This iteration removed callback, stream, output, and host-presentation parameters from application, direct JavaScript, and MCP stdio operation methods. The review follow-up also removed FactoryEventConsumer from InvocationOperation and StartSync, moving live subscription and final reconciliation into the injected OpeningPresentationOwner behind a typed InvocationTarget.EventScopeID. Canonical Wire constructs one process-scoped owner; CLI and MCP adapters register transport-local scopes and pass only typed IDs with immutable selections. Focused owner, Factory Sessions, CLI run, Wire, runtime-opening, typecheck, and wire-smoke tests pass; no customer-facing OpenAPI contract changed.

userStories.title: Own dynamic log and metric scopes privately
userStories.description: As an operator running multiple Factory Sessions, I want each session's log and metric files selected by the injected observability owners so that destinations remain isolated without creating per-session logger or recorder services.
acceptanceCriteria: The injected logging and metrics implementations open destination-specific private scope state from values and opaque session/runtime IDs; operation callers do not supply or receive a logger, recorder, or factory.
Two sessions using the same injected observability roots write to their intended collision-free destinations without cross-session records, truncation, or scope leakage.
Closing or failing one session closes its private observability scopes exactly once and does not close the shared observability root or the other session's scopes.
Destination creation and file writes occur only when the owning operation opens or records to a scope, never during BuildProcess construction.
Invalid or unwritable destinations return actionable owner errors without reporting the session as cleanly ready and without leaking a partially opened scope.
Focused observability scope, close, and failure tests pass, including concurrent or race coverage where scope state is shared.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented process-scoped RuntimeLogOwner and RuntimeMetricsOwner contracts. Canonical Wire now constructs each owner once with the base logger, artifact clock, collision ID generator, and path reserver; RuntimeFactory.Build opens private scopes from value-only destination selections and opaque session/runtime IDs without receiving a logger or sink factory. Log and metrics scopes are wrapped in close-once guards, so failure or repeated cleanup closes only the affected scope exactly once while the shared owners and sibling scopes remain usable. Added owner construction inertness, collision-free path, session isolation, sibling-scope-after-close, unwritable-destination, value-forwarding, nil-owner, and close-once tests; regenerated wire_gen.go. Focused Factory Runtime/Wire suites and wire-smoke pass. Story 006 remains for the end-to-end inert/reusable process proof.

userStories.title: Prove inert reusable process behavior end to end
userStories.description: As a customer reusing one built process, I want process construction to be inert and repeated session execution to preserve established behavior so that build-time injection does not start work early or change runtime outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Constructing a valid process performs no Factory Session start, runtime activation, provider/worker command, watcher/subprocess start, dynamic observability-file creation, or recording append on instrumented injected edges.
After explicit execution, two session starts reuse the same injected root and edge identities while producing distinct session/runtime IDs and isolated results, events, and observability scopes.
Representative successful and failed Factory Session flows retain their characterized terminal result, canonical Factory Event ordering, response behavior, and edge-call cardinality.
Construction failure unwinds only construction-owned resources and leaves no operation-scoped goroutine, file, scope, subprocess, watcher, or session record behind.
The P1 deletion-register rows are updated to reflect only replacements actually live in this packet; deferred P2-P6 removals are not claimed complete and no compatibility factory is added.
Focused root-process functional, inertness, repeated-session, and failure-path tests pass using deterministic observation rather than sleeps.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
